articles.title: Chinese carmaker BYD’s offices in Netherlands raided over JLR ‘copycat car’ claim
articles.summary: Bailiffs reportedly seized digital records before court case over alleged intellectual property breaches on Land Rover Defender Bailiffs acting for Jaguar Land Rover raided the Dutch offices of a…

blocks.text: Bailiffs acting for Jaguar Land Rover raided the Dutch offices of a Chinese “copycat” rival before a legal showdown this week over whether its “Defender clone” infringes intellectual property rights.
Bailiffs acting on behalf of JLR reportedly seized digital records from the offices of Chinese carmaker BYD in Schiedam and Hoofddorp in August, according to the Sunday Times.

The raid took place before a court case in the The Hague this week which will decide whether the BYD has a case to answer over allegations that its Ti7 SUV infringes the intellectual property of the Land Rover Defender.

Motoring experts have likened BYD’s seven-seat plug-in hybrid SUV to the Defender since it went on sale in China in September last year. The company is scheduled to launch the vehicle, which the BBC’s Top Gear magazine called the “Chinese Defender clone”, in the UK market in January at a price of £47,995, undercutting the Defender by more than £20,000.
BYD says on its website that “an unapologetically boxy profile delivers the imposing, chunky design that finds favour among SUV buyers, yet delivers a contemporary look”.

blocks.caption: BYD electric vehicles awaiting export to Brazil at Lianyungang port in Jiangsu province, China. Photograph: China Daily/Reuters

blocks.text: The price of JLR’s seven-seat Defender 110 starts from £68,465and is one of the country’s bestselling cars. The UK-based carmaker, which is owned by India’s Tata Motors, sold 29,500 Defenders to retail customers between July and September this year, compared with 25,370a year earlier.

The raid in the Netherlands was carried out by court-ordered bailiffs, with JLR suspecting that BYD reverse-engineered some of the technology that could be used in the Ti7, the Times reported. JLR wanted to secure the digital records before they could be destroyed.
JLR and BYD declined to comment on the “ongoing legal proceedings”.

The dispute with BYD is not the first legal case JLR has pursed against a Chinese company over copycat allegations. It won a legal case to stop Jiangling Motor Corporation selling a copycat vehicle in 2019 after a three-year court battle.
after newsletter promotion

In some cases JLR has taken a collaborative approach to dealing with the rise of China’s carmakers. It agreed to form a joint venture with Chery in a 2012 deal which later included licensing its discontinued Freelander brand with the company.

Chery’s Jaecoo model, which is not part of the joint venture, has been called the Temu Range Rover because of its similarities to the JLR vehicle after years of collaboration between the pair. It costs £10,000 less than JLR’s Range Rover.

The Jaecoo was the bestselling car in the UK in October, with 10,813 registrations, taking its market share from 2.07% to 4.30%, according to the Society of Motor Manufacturers & Traders. JLR’s sales of the Range Rover fell to 43,300 in the third quarter of this year, from 47,196 cars sold in the same months last year.

articles.title: Egypt train crash leaves several dead, over 100 injured
articles.summary: A train derailed after colliding with another train south of Cairo, with authorities confirming several deaths and saying more than 100 passengers were injured. Over 50 ambulances were deployed to…

image.caption: Scores of people were reported injured in the train collision Image: AFP

blocks.text: At least seven people were killed in the train collision in Egypt on Sunday, with authorities also confirming over 100 people were injured.

The collision involved one train hitting the rear end of another while traveling through the Giza province on the line between Cairo and the southern Nile city of Aswan. One of the trains then derailed and several cars flipped, according to the Egyptian authorities.

blocks.caption: Authorities said rescue teams and cleanup crews were deployed to the siteImage: AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: Officials said 52 ambulances were deployed to the scene some 52 kilometers (32 miles) south of Cairo. Emergency crews and cranes were also working to clear the line and restore railway traffic through Giza's al-Ayyat district.
The cause of the accident was not immediately clear.
El-Sissi says incident being investigated
In a social media post, Egyptian President Abdel-Fattah el-Sissi said he ordered an investigation. He also urged the state agencies to "hold accountable anyone found to have been negligent."

blocks.caption: State media reports indicated a large number of injuriesImage: AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: The crash tool place in the same area as the worst train disaster in Egypt's history, which saw over 370 people were killed in a train fire in 2002. Several crashes also claimed dozens of lives in the same region in 2009.

In recent years, Egypt has invested billions of dollars into new highways and high-speed rail lines, but is still facing safety issues and repeated crashes while attempting to revamp its aging rail network.

articles.title: Expanded Bayanihan SIM project eyed
articles.summary: The Private Sector Advisory Council (PSAC) is pushing for the expansion of the Bayanihan SIM Project, which provides free internet access to students, teachers and low-income families in far-flung…

blocks.text: November 9, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — The Private Sector Advisory Council (PSAC) is pushing for the expansion of the Bayanihan SIM Project, which provides free internet access to students, teachers and low-income families in far-flung and underserved areas.

As of Oct. 14, the program had distributed 929,259 SIM cards to beneficiaries from the Department of Education and Department of Social Welfare and Development and connected 2,810 schools across the country. Its coverage now extends to 76 provinces and 404 municipalities.

“Building on this progress, PSAC is recommending the extension of Bayanihan SIM subscriptions to help ensure that more than one million intended beneficiaries can continue accessing online learning, government services and other essential digital tools,” PSAC said in a statement over the weekend.
PSAC-Digital Infrastructure Sector Group made the recommendation to President Marcos during their meeting at Malacañang last week.
The council is seeking government support to secure the necessary funding and sustain the program, particularly for communities where reliable internet access remains a challenge.

Marcos recognized that many Filipinos, particularly those living in remote communities, continue to struggle with weak or nonexistent internet connections, limiting their access to essential services and economic opportunities.
According to Malacañang, the President is personally reviewing the progress of the Bayanihan SIM Project to explore ways to expand its reach and connect more Filipinos.
“The President is also seeking stronger private-sector participation to accelerate the development of digital infrastructure nationwide,” the Presidential Communications Office earlier said.

Spearheaded by the Department of Information and Communications Technology, the Bayanihan SIM program provides beneficiaries with a SIM card that includes 25 gigabytes of monthly data valid for one year.

articles.title: Department of Agriculture bans imported pork cuts
articles.summary: The Department of Agriculture (DA) has banned the entry of various imported pork cuts, as its investigation found that continued imports cause injury to the country’s hog industry.

blocks.text: November 9, 2026 | 12:00am
The agency has imposed quantitative restrictions on nine pork cut varieties for 60 days as a provisional safeguard measure, according to Department Order 33.
STAR / File

MANILA, Philippines — The Department of Agriculture (DA) has banned the entry of various imported pork cuts, as its investigation found that continued imports cause injury to the country’s hog industry.
Included in the ban are fresh, chilled and frozen swine carcasses and half carcasses; bone-in ham, shoulders and cuts; and fresh, chilled and frozen edible offal and liver.
Quantitative restrictions are trade measures that a country imposes to limit the import or export of a specific commodity or item.

The department said prima facie evidence showed that surging pork imports were a substantial cause of serious injury to local hog raisers and that any delay in intervention could result in irreparable damage to the industry.

“Increased imports translated into significantly rising higher market share and significantly declining self-sufficiency ratio during the period of investigation that crowded out local production over the years,” the DA said.
This comes after the agency conducted a safeguard measures investigation for 2021 to 2025.
The agency has found that pork import surged by 42 percent to 836,239.91 metric tons in 2025 from 589,674.59 MT in 2023.
It added that imports made up a growing portion of the country’s pork supply, increasing to 61 percent in 2025 from 39 percent in 2021.
The agency stressed that the country’s self sufficiency ratio for pork declined to 65.5 percent in 2025 from 74.3 percent in 2021.
“Excessive imports and frozen stock buildups caused farmgate prices to collapse in 2026,” the DA said.

articles.title: Bill vs AI job displacement filed
articles.summary: Amid growing concerns over automation-driven layoffs, Sen. Erwin Tulfo has filed a bill seeking to amend the Labor Code to protect Filipino workers from being displaced by artificial intelligence…

blocks.text: November 9, 2026 | 12:00am

This illustration photograph taken in Helsinki on June 12, 2023, shows an AI (Artificial Intelligence) logo blended with four fake Twitter accounts bearing profile pictures apparently generated by Artificial Intelligence software.
Olivier MORIN / AFP

MANILA, Philippines — Amid growing concerns over automation-driven layoffs, Sen. Erwin Tulfo has filed a bill seeking to amend the Labor Code to protect Filipino workers from being displaced by artificial intelligence (AI).
Senate Bill No. 2563 establishes strict guidelines for AI-related retrenchments, mandating companies to prioritize reskilling programs for their workforce before resorting to job cuts.
“As companies adopt AI, employees whose jobs become redundant risk losing not only their employment but also their means of supporting their families,” Tulfo said.
“Technological progress is inevitable, but Filipino workers should not be left behind or made to bear its costs alone,” he added.

Under the proposed measure, employers intending to implement AI systems that could lead to workforce reduction must notify the Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE) at least six months in advance.

The bill sets specific conditions for lawful termination due to automation. The AI integration must be a bona fide implementation done in good faith for valid economic reasons, such as cost reduction or enhanced efficiency.
Furthermore, layoffs must be the absolute last resort and the selection of employees to be dismissed must follow fair and reasonable criteria.

Should retrenchment be unavoidable, displaced workers would be entitled to a higher separation pay equivalent to at least two months’ salary, or two months’ pay for every year of service, whichever is higher.
“There must be a proactive effort to keep workers away from termination just because AI comes in,” Tulfo, who chairs the Senate committee on social justice, welfare and rural development, stated.

articles.title: Stronger measures vs school violence pushed
articles.summary: Financial technology lending company JuanHand is pushing for stronger preventive measures and greater public awareness of school-related violence amid a string of incidents in recent months.

Students undergo entrance security checks at Parañaque National High School–Main during the visit of Education Secretary Sonny Angara on June 26, 2026.
Department of Education via Facebook

MANILA, Philippines — Financial technology lending company JuanHand is pushing for stronger preventive measures and greater public awareness of school-related violence amid a string of incidents in recent months.
JuanHand president and CEO Francisco Mauricio said there is a need for a stronger response against cases of nihilistic violent extremism.
NVE is an emerging internet subculture in which vulnerable individuals, often minors, are groomed and manipulated into committing real-world violence.
“We want to create awareness about this problem, which can actually grow very big if we’re not careful,” Mauricio said.

To help broaden awareness of the issue, JuanHand and the University of Asia and the Pacific organized a forum last Nov. 6, which brought together government agencies, experts and cybersecurity specialists to discuss emerging threats affecting children and students.

articles.title: P2 million escrow, fines eyed over balikbayan boxes
articles.summary: The Bureau of Customs (BOC) is seeking to impose a mandatory deposit of at least P2 million in an escrow account of cargo deconsolidators alongside hefty fines for delivery failures, in order to…

blocks.text: November 9, 2026 | 12:00am
Under the draft customs administrative order, deconsolidators accredited with other government agencies and who wish to conduct business with the agency shall apply for registration.
Steffano Oppo from Corelens

MANILA, Philippines — The Bureau of Customs (BOC) is seeking to impose a mandatory deposit of at least P2 million in an escrow account of cargo deconsolidators alongside hefty fines for delivery failures, in order to safeguard balikbayan boxes sent home by overseas Filipino workers (OFWs).

To guarantee compliance, the deconsolidator and agency should open an escrow account with a BOC-nominated trust bank, with a required deposit of about P2 million and an additional P500,000 for each consolidator in each country of operation.
Unregistered entities operating as deconsolidators face a P300,000 fine for the first offense and blacklisting for the second.
Forwarders that fail to process, clear or deliver balikbayan boxes to ultimate consignees without a valid justification will face immediate suspension until reactivated by Customs.

articles.title: DFA rejects ombudsman’s remarks on visa issuance
articles.summary: The Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) yesterday rejected Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla’s “erroneous” statement that authority over visa matters belongs exclusively to…

blocks.text: November 9, 2026 | 12:00am

“The DFA strongly objects to Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla’s assertions that authority over visa matters belongs exclusively to immigration authorities under the Department of Justice (DOJ), that the DFA merely exercises delegated powers, and that no other law confers such authority upon the DFA,” the DFA said in a statement.
STAR / File

MANILA, Philippines — The Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) yesterday rejected Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla’s “erroneous” statement that authority over visa matters belongs exclusively to immigration authorities.
“The DFA’s visa-issuance authority is founded on law. It is neither derived from nor dependent upon delegation by the DOJ,” it added.

The DFA again cited Section 21(3), Chapter 7 (The Foreign Service), Title I, Book IV of Executive Order No. 292, or the Administrative Code of 1987, which expressly recognizes visa issuance as a statutory function of Philippine consular offices.

The mandate is recognized under Articles 3, 5(d) and 70 of the Vienna Convention on Consular Relations, which establish visa issuance as a consular function that may be exercised by diplomatic missions.
Remulla said the visa processing should be transferred from the DFA to a third party service provider such as VFS Global.

While the provider may provide administrative support in receiving and facilitating visa applications, the DFA reiterated that the authority to assess, approve or deny Philippine visas is a “sovereign governmental function that cannot be transferred to a private entity through an outsourcing arrangement.”
Remulla cited a Chinese businessman’s comment that a Philippine business visa is more difficult to obtain compared to another country.

The DFA emphasized that each country exercises sovereign authority to prescribe its own visa requirements and procedures. It called out the false information and irresponsible comments made about passport services.
“The DFA does not issue “fake” passports nor does it impose documentary requirements to make applications deliberately difficult,” it said.
All documents required from passport applicants are provided under Republic Act 11983 or the New Passport Law and its Implementing Rules and Regulations.
“The prevention of passport fraud is precisely why documentary safeguards and identity verification requirements are necessary,” the DFA said.
It added that there were also insinuations made during Remulla’s program “Executive Session” on radio dzRH that the DFA’s passport and visa services are commercial undertakings.
“The DFA firmly rejects any suggestion that the Department treats passports and visas as commodities for sale,” the DFA said.
Passport and visa fees, it said, are collected pursuant to the prescribed government schedule of fees and form part of government revenue.

articles.title: PNP tracking down Thomas Markle’s accomplices
articles.summary: The Philippine National Police (PNP) is intensifying efforts to identify possible local accomplices, including those who may have facilitated or participated in the crimes of American Thomas Markle…

blocks.text: November 9, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — The Philippine National Police (PNP) is intensifying efforts to identify possible local accomplices, including those who may have facilitated or participated in the crimes of American Thomas Markle who is accused of sexually exploiting children.
PNP chief Gen. Jose Melencio Nartatez Jr. said investigators are working to establish the extent of Markle’s activities in the country and determine whether he had local associates.
“Child exploitation is not the work of one person alone. Others enable, facilitate or profit from the abuse. We will pursue every lead and identify everyone involved,” Nartatez said.
He added that the PNP’s responsibility “is not only to hold the principal suspect accountable but also to dismantle the network that allows these crimes to happen.”

Markle, 82, was arrested in Florida over possession of child sexual abuse materials, including photographs of himself with naked minors. He appeared before US magistrate judge Thomas Wilson at a courthouse in Tampa, Florida.
Police earlier reported that three memory cards and a cellphone turned over by Markle’s son contained child sexual abuse material.

Nartatez urged people who may have been victimized by Markle to come forward and file formal complaints, saying their accounts could help strengthen the case against the suspect and identify other people involved.

articles.title: GenCorp lawyer skips impeachment hearing today
articles.summary: Vice President Sara Duterte’s defense team yesterday confirmed that one of their witnesses, GenCorp Industries Inc. corporate counsel Suzette Balucanag-Punay would be unable to attend the…

blocks.text: November 9, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — Vice President Sara Duterte’s defense team yesterday confirmed that one of their witnesses, GenCorp Industries Inc. corporate counsel Suzette Balucanag-Punay would be unable to attend the impeachment hearing today.

“We confirm that Atty. Suzette Balucanag-Punay informed us that she will be unable to attend tomorrow’s hearing due to a previously scheduled MRI (magnetic resonance imaging),” defense spokesman Michael Poa said in a message to The STAR yesterday.
However, he clarified that the witness would only be absent today. She has been scheduled to appear before the impeachment court from Nov. 9-13.
The impeachment trial is scheduled to resume today, with the defense team’s turn to present its witnesses and evidence.

Poa said the defense team recognizes “that her (Punay) health and well-being must take priority,” and that they have already “promptly filed the necessary manifestation before the (Senate) impeachment court.”
In her statement of assets, liability and net worth from 2016 to 2025, Duterte listed herself as an incorporator or stockholder of GenCorp Industries.

However, her name reportedly did not appear as an incorporator or stockholder of GenCorp in its Articles of Incorporation and General Information Sheets submitted to the Securities and Exchange Commission from 2020 to 2025.
Earlier, political and constitutional law professor Ralph Sarmiento begged off to appear as the first witness of the defense, saying he wanted to keep his views and opinions independent.
Prosecution scores defense witness list
Meanwhile, the prosecution panel criticized some of the names in the defense’s witness list for having nothing to do with the alleged unexplained wealth of the Vice President.

“For example, a Quezon City prosecutor (Vimar Barcellano) was named as one of the witnesses, but there was no indication at all with regard to the purpose on why is he being called,” private prosecutor Benjamin Tolosa Jr. said during a weekly news forum in Quezon City over the weekend.
“And there was also another witness from the banks. But there was no explanation at all on why his testimony is important,” he noted.
The Duterte camp initially submitted a list of 25 intended witnesses for the impeachment trial. — Delon Porcalla

articles.title: Philippines moves to address climate-related loss, damage
articles.summary: The Philippines is advancing a strategic and coordinated response to climate-related loss and damage through the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR), the Climate Change Commission…

blocks.text: November 9, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — The Philippines is advancing a strategic and coordinated response to climate-related loss and damage through the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR), the Climate Change Commission and the United Nations Development Program.
The initiative aims to build a coordinated national framework and long-term action agenda for communities facing the growing impacts of climate change.
“The country is working to translate international momentum into concrete actions that help communities address the compounding and cascading climate impacts,” DENR chief Juan Miguel Cuna said.

“The Philippines is developing a national Climate-related Loss and Damage Framework and Strategy that will guide how government, development partners and other stakeholders work together to support communities affected by climate impacts. The strategy seeks to strengthen coordination, improve access to financing, enhance knowledge and data systems, and ensure that assistance reaches those most affected,” Cuna said.

MANILA, Philippines — Typhoon Samuel is set to enter the Philippine area of responsibility (PAR) today, according to the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration.
It was packing winds of 120 kilometers per hour and gusts of 150 kph while moving west-northwestward at 20 kph.
Samuel is expected to enter PAR early today but will not affect the country’s weather conditions or make landfall.

articles.title: Israel: Eisenkot officially tasked with forming a government
articles.summary: Israeli President Isaac Herzog tasked Gadi Eisenkot with the right of trying to form a government. The opposition leader's way to replacing Benjamin Netanyahu as prime minister is full of political…

image.caption: Isaac Herzog (right) said that he expected Gadi Eisenkot to do his best to form a government that would serve all parts of the Israeli peopleImage: Ronen Zvulun/REUTERS

blocks.text: Israel President Isaac Herzog has officially tasked Gadi Eisenkot with forming a government.

Eisenkot, the head of the centrist Yashar party, will have 28 days to secure a coalition to replace current Prime MinisterBenjamin Netanyahu's religious-nationalist government, with Herzog having the authority to prolong Eisenkot's mandate by 14 days.

"The conversations with the different parties were open and transparent, while also resurfacing the many voices in Israeli society. They reminded us the fact that all Israeli citizens have an equal voice, from all parts of society," Herzog said.
He stressed that Eisenkot received the clearest support from the majority of Knesset members when it comes to the question of forming the next government.

"The challenges we face are giant. Iran is not waiting a second in its threats. We have to start building a future in the region and proceed with Trump's 20-point plan in Gaza, as well as negotiating the future with Lebanon and other neighbors," the Israeli president said, adding that "Israel needs a stable government that faces these challenges."
Herzog said that he expected Eisenkot to do his best to form a government that would serve all parts of the Israeli people.
In turn, Eisenkot stressed that he is committed to establishing a national emergency government.
"We do not have the privilege of endless rounds of elections. I will send an official approach to all of the Knesset's members, as parties and individuals, for talks," he added.
What do we know about coalition forming

Yashar was Israel's second biggest party in Israel's October elections with 21 parliament seats, behind Netanyahu's Likud with 27. However, more members of the Knesset, the Israeli parliament, recommended Eisenkot as the man who should be given the first right to try and secure a government.

In comparison to Eisenkot's 67 recommendations, Netanyahu received the backing of 46 members, with the ultraorthodox Ashkenazi party United Torah Judaism (UTJ) deciding not to make any recommendations despite having joined Netanyahu's governments of the past 17 years.
Should Eisenkot fail to form a coalition, President Isaac Herzog will have the authority to pass the task on to a different Knesset member, with the second person in line expected to be Netanyahu.

If the Likud leader, too, will not manage to form a government, and if no other parliament member will claim to have enough support to head a government, Israel will likely head to another round of elections.
Coalition forming is a difficult task
Dividing Israel's Zionist parties into blocs results in Netanyahu's religious-nationalist allies receiving 53 seats, with the Eisenkot-led anti-Netanyahu bloc having 48 seats.

Israel's two Arab parties, which with 19 seats received historic support due to the high turnout in Arab and Palestinian communities, already voiced their willingness to support the Zionist opposition in ousting Netanyahu and his government. Mostly the religious Muslim party Ra'am, led by Mansour Abbas, said it is willing to join a coalition once again in a bid to improve Israel's Arab and Palestinian communities' lives.
In 2021, Ra'am made history in becoming the first-ever Arab party to join an Israeli coalition, signing an agreement with right-wing candidate Naftali Bennet and liberal politician Yair Lapid.

The other Arab party, the Joint List, is a union of several smaller parties. While its members have never joined an Israeli coalition, its politicians did provide political support for an Israeli government from the opposition during Yitzhak Rabin's second term as prime minister as his government pushed through the Oslo Accords with the Palestinians, a term which was cut short by Rabin's murder in November 1995.
Israeli President asks Eisenkot to form government
Campaign promises at risk

Both sides of Israel's Zionist political divide promised not to rely on votes by Arab parties to form a coalition, meaning Eisenkot's bloc will have to track back on one of its election promises to form a government with them.

However, a poll by the Accord Center of the Hebrew University in Jerusalem carried out two days after the elections found that 59 percent of Israel's Zionist opposition voters would rather have a government with Ra'am, and with the Joint List's abstention, than any other alternative.

Another option touted by Israeli media in the past week was the country's two ultraorthodox parties potentially joining an Eisenkot-led coalition. UTJ and Sepharadi party Shas have seven seats each, but a coalition with any of them would require Eisenkot to backtrack on another campaign promise: to pass through a legislation to secure the army conscription of young ultraorthodox men, which the two parties strictly object, citing fears over the future of religious studies in Israel.

Moreover, Shas supporters are known to hold right-wing views favorable to Netanyahu, with party head Arye Deri being considered as one of the politicians closest to Israel's longest-serving prime minister.
Effects on Palestinians
The government formed is bound to have wide-ranging implications on the lives of Palestinians in the Occupied West Bank and the Gaza Strip.

The Netanyahu-led current coalition also includes far-right parties Otzma Yehudit and Religious Zionism, which received 13 seats in the October election. The two parties support annexing the West Bank — a territory considered illegally occupied by Israel according to international law — as well as re-establishing Israeli settlements in the Gaza Strip and carrying out the so-called "wilful migration," the plan to move Gaza's 2.1 million Palestinians to other countries. Large parts of Netanyahu's Likud, too, support the plan.
The two parties often provide political backing to the violent settlers carrying out attacks against Palestinians in the Occupied West Bank.

Eisenkot himself promised to secure a Gaza Strip without Hamas rule within 18 months of becoming prime minister. This stands in contrast to the Netanyahu government's current policy of allowing Hamas to control certain parts of the enclave, despite the US-brokered ceasefire agreement saying a board of technocrats should take over Gaza from Hamas.

While Gadi Eisenkot's bloc includes several right-wing parties, their positions differ from those of Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition. Naftali Bennet, the head of the opposition's second biggest party Beyachad, labels himself as a right-winger and a supporter of settlements.

However, he has repeatedly used strong terms to condemn settler attacks on Palestinians. Eisenkot himself, too, condemned settler violence towards Palestinians, saying they are the result of the Netanyahu government's policies.

articles.title: Two police officers hailed as heroes for confronting Kraków gunman
articles.summary: Jakub Kulik critically injured and Artur Morański also wounded after actions that ‘prevented further casualties’ Two Polish police officers who were injured as they pursued and detained the gunman in…

blocks.text: Two Polish police officers who were injured as they pursued and detained the gunman in Kraków on Saturday have been hailed as heroes.

One of them is Jakub Kulik, a former paratrooper and volunteer firefighter, who was left critically injured after a close-range exchange of fire with the suspect, a 24-year-old Polish national who killed six and injured 17 in an attack believed to have been inspired by far-right ideologies.
The other injured police officer is Artur Morański. Both are under 30 years old, the Polish news network TVP World reported.
Poland’s prime minister, Donald Tusk, said on Saturday in a post on X: “They probably saved many human lives, disregarding the risk to their own.”
The Polish justice minister, Waldemar Żurek, said the rapid response and heroism of the two police officers “prevented further human casualties”.
Police arrived at the scene 23 seconds after receiving the first emergency call from Kraków’s main square, where the suspect was shooting at random from his car.

Footage that emerged on Sunday showed two police officers exchanging fire with the gunman. One of the officers then apprehended the suspect on the ground before firing his own weapon several times. The officer then fell down, apparently injured himself.
Kulik, from the southern Polish city of Bielsko-Biala, was hit by three bullets and underwent surgery on Saturday. There has been a national appeal for blood donors.
Morański was shot in the chest area and also underwent surgery. Both men were brought out of medically induced comas on Sunday, Polskie Radio 24 reported.

Kulik is also a member of the volunteer fire service in Bielsko-Biala. “We’re very proud of him,” a volunteer firefighter from the city’s Leszczyny district told the local news website Bielsko.biala.pl. “He responds to emergencies just like we do.”

TVP World reported that Morański was from Powroźnik, a village about 90 miles (150km) south-east of Krakow and close to the border with Slovakia. A mass was held for him at the local church on Sunday.

articles.title: Thousands remain without power after second windstorm wallops B.C.
articles.summary: Thousands of people woke up without power in British Columbia on Sunday in the wake of a second powerful windstorm blowing off the Pacific Ocean.

image.caption: A windsock blows in strong winds in Burrard Inlet between Vancouver and the North Shore. Hundreds of thousands of people lost power across B.C. overnight following a second powerful windstorm this weekend. (CBC)

blocks.text: British Columbia
Thousands of people woke up without power in British Columbia on Sunday in the wake of a second powerful windstorm blowing off the Pacific Ocean.
Wind warnings remain in effect for B.C.'s South Coast and Central Interior
Thousands of people woke up without power in British Columbia on Sunday in the wake of a second windstorm blowing off the Pacific Ocean.

As of Sunday morning, more than 63,000 B.C. Hydro customers were without electricity, more than half of them in the Lower Mainland and Sunshine Coast — down from about 135,000 across the province at the peak of the storm.
B.C. Hydro said the hardest hit areas include Surrey, Duncan, Port Hardy and Prince George.
Wind warnings remain in effect for Metro Vancouver, the Fraser Valley, the Sunshine Coast and all of Vancouver Island south of Seward.
Environment and Climate Change Canada has also issued wind warnings for the Central Interior, including the Prince George, Stuart-Nechacko and Lakes district areas.
The agency says gusts of up to 90 km/h are possible.
Highway 10 was closed between 180 and 184 Street in Surrey overnight due to downed electrical wires, but has since reopened to one lane.

articles.title: Homes and temples glow across India to mark Diwali
articles.summary: Millions of Indians are marking the festival of lights with glowing lamps, fireworks and traditional sweets.

blocks.text: Millions across India are celebrating Diwali, the Hindu festival of lights, illuminating homes, temples, offices and streets with oil lamps and colourful lights to symbolise the triumph of light over darkness.
The festival falls on the darkest night of the Hindu lunar month of Kartik, when the moon is not visible in the sky.
Although Diwali traditions vary across India's regions and communities, the festival is widely marked by prayers, family gatherings, the exchange of sweets and the lighting of firecrackers.
But the celebrations come amid growing concerns over air pollution, particularly in northern India.
Seasonal weather conditions and the burning of crop residue contribute to deteriorating air quality, while firecrackers set off during Diwali can make the situation worse.

Air pollution in the Indian capital Delhi has reached such hazardous levels that it is the most polluted Diwali festival in a decade. New measures to improve air quality do not seem to have been successful.
India's financial capital, Mumbai, has also experienced high pollution levels in recent weeks.
In an effort to limit pollution, India's Supreme Court on Monday permitted the manufacture, sale and use of certified "green" firecrackers in Delhi and surrounding areas for a limited period.

These firecrackers are designed to produce 20-30% fewer emissions than conventional fireworks. But critics have questioned how effective they are at reducing pollution and raised concerns that conventional firecrackers could still make their way into the capital from neighbouring states.

articles.title: Weakening AI copyright law will spell ‘disaster for creativity’, global music body warns Albanese
articles.summary: Exclusive: Head of IFPI says allowing AI companies access to online content would be a ‘huge mistake’ and damage Australia’s reputation Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast…

blocks.text: Australia weakening copyright protections for AI companies would be “ridiculous and dangerous”, the global peak body for the music recording industry has warned as it watches with concern how the Albanese government responds to big tech’s demands.

While local creatives have raised constitutional issues and threatened political backlash, the International Federation of the Phonographic Industry (IFPI), representing recording industry bodies worldwide, said its members were worried about Australia potentially agreeing to demands other nations had rejected.

“Why would Australia do this? Why would a sophisticated, democratic country that has a phenomenal cultural power of its own, choose to make this very odd decision and buy into the promises of a few large AI companies, and throw away their own culture and creativity?” Victoria Oakley, the CEO of IFPI, told Guardian Australia.

“I don’t think Australia wants to be the weakest link in this situation, the one that believed the promises and gave in and threw creativity under the bus on behalf of everyone else. That doesn’t feel very Australian to me.

“You just need one safe harbour, because then you can train on music from anywhere in the world. So this isn’t just about Australian music and Australian culture; it’s about music and culture everywhere.”

Labor is mulling copyright changes in a suite of policy overhauls around AI, including datacentres, online safety, workforce, energy and the economy. While the prime minister, Anthony Albanese, promised “the strongest possible protection”, warning it would be “theft” if creatives weren’t paid for their work, creative industries were alarmed after AI companies requested a weakening of copyright law to train on Australian material.

Some AI companies have rejected making licensing agreements under existing copyright law, saying it was too difficult. Anthropic suggested an “opt-out” model that would allow it to scrape content unless rights holders signalled an objection.
Large AI companies say they need legal certainty on issues like copyright before making investments in Australia or training their models here.
Oakley said AI companies had made similar proposals in the US, UK and other nations and that Australia should not accept such a bargain.
“I just don’t think it’s true that you will only get investment or growth, or be seen as pro-innovation, if you entirely give in to the demands of AI companies,” Oakley said.
“We’ve been talking to capitals around the world, saying ‘are you seeing what’s going on in Australia?’ We think this is a disaster for creativity.”

The attorney general, Michelle Rowland, said via a spokesperson last week that the government was “committed to supporting” creatives and pledged that “any future copyright changes deliver meaningful control and fair compensation”.
Oakley said she worried about AI and copyright “everywhere”, but feared “Australia appears to be threatening to do something really ridiculous and dangerous.”
She said creative industries worried about “contagion” of copyright relaxation if Australia caved in, and that copyright material from anywhere in the world could be affected.

She declined to speculate on any potential legal or constitutional challenges, as raised by the Australian Recording Industry Association, but said it would be reputational damage to Australia’s standing in the creative world.
“It would be a huge mistake, and I think the prize is not worth what you’re throwing away,” she said.

In recent answers to a parliamentary committee on AI, responding to questions from the independent senator David Pocock about why it couldn’t replicate the kind of deals Spotify had made, OpenAI said the music streaming giant “has a different business, where it primarily transmits un-transformed copyrighted content, so would be expected to license content that it streams”.
But Oakley said music labels had already inked dozens of licensing deals with smaller AI companies around the world.

“It is perfectly possible to license. I’m almost shocked that these words are coming out of the mouths of some of the larger AI companies … We already know how to license music to tech platforms because that’s exactly how Spotify works, or Amazon Music, Apple, or Tidal,” she said.

“You have a ready, willing set of rights holders who want to license with a history of licensing in the streaming world, but also current evidence of licensing to AI firms. Let’s let the market do what it needs to do. Come to us and we’ll make it work.”

articles.title: Hadden Kelloway once considered leaving Sparwood, B.C. Now he's mayor
articles.summary: Hadden Kelloway once feared he wouldn't be accepted in Sparwood, B.C. Friends and neighbours convinced him to stay. Now, more than 30 years after arriving, he's the town's mayor.

image.caption: Hadden Kelloway practises his inaugural speech at home before being sworn in as Sparwood's new mayor on Nov. 3, 2026. (Amber Wang/CBC)

blocks.text: British Columbia
Hadden Kelloway once feared he wouldn't be accepted in Sparwood, B.C. Friends and neighbours convinced him to stay. Now, more than 30 years after arriving, he's the town's mayor.
Kelloway once considered moving away to transition. More than a decade later, he leads the community
Hours before his swearing-in ceremony, Hadden Kelloway stood in front of a mirror at home, practising a speech he would soon deliver as the new mayor of Sparwood, B.C.
On Nov. 3, he took his oath of office in the small southeastern B.C. mining town where he has lived for more than three decades.
It was a moment he once could hardly have imagined.
Kelloway made history on Oct. 17, becoming B.C.'s first known openly transgender mayor.
He received 864 votes, compared with 334 for acting mayor Amy Cardozo.
His victory also marks a changing of the guard in Sparwood's local politics. The small mining town had been led for years by David Wilks, a former federal Conservative MP who stepped down in May.
Kelloway defeated his interim successor, while five of the six council seats went to newcomers.
Hadden Kelloway shows a tattoo he got after undergoing top surgery. He says it depicts a man trying to break free from a woman's body. (Amber Wang/CBC)
A community he almost left

After moving from Newfoundland, Kelloway planned to spend five years in Sparwood. He stayed for the friendships and tight-knit community. But when he decided to transition about 15 years ago, he found himself weighing a major decision.
"I felt that maybe a small town like Sparwood wasn't ready for it," he said.
He considered moving to Vancouver, Calgary or Edmonton, where he could go through his transition without people knowing his history.
Instead, conversations with family, friends and a colleague convinced him to stay.
After he told friends at his curling club about his plans, one put a unisex sign on the washroom door.
"I knew then that this is where I was going to stay at that moment," he said.
Later, staff at the local swimming pool made sure he had access to suitable changing rooms when he wanted to return to swimming.
Penny Lowe, who met Kelloway through a hockey team 32 years ago, was among the friends who supported him.
"To me it's the exact same person and nothing has changed for me," Lowe said.
Hadden Kelloway, left, and longtime friend Penny Lowe. The two met through a hockey team 32 years ago. (Amber Wang/CBC)
A new mayor, and calls for change
"That feeling of acceptance is undescribable," Kelloway said. "Now, when you get that town that accepts you to elect you as mayor ... It's an unbelievable feeling."
Preparing for the swearing-in ceremony also brought a personal first.
"The lady at the mall asked me what size of suit I took when I graduated school and I told her I had no idea. I actually wore a dress when I graduated." Kelloway said.
But Kelloway says taking office also means addressing what he heard during the campaign.
Residents told him they felt their local council wasn't listening.
"We lost that togetherness somewhere along the way," he said.
Kelloway says that he wants to create a closer relationship between councillors and district staff and local organisations.
For Lowe, the election carries its own expectations.
"I don't think there's going to be anything that's going to be hidden away from the people and everyone's going to know and have that voice and then it'll be answered," she said.

items: More stories from the B.C. Interior

blocks.text: Hadden Kelloway took the oath of office as Sparwood's new mayor on Nov. 3, 2026. He won the election with 864 votes. (Amber Wang/CBC)
More than a personal milestone
"They did not cast their vote for what I was. Sparwood cast their vote for who I was," Kelloway said.
Although Kelloway has spoken publicly about his transition, he did not campaign on his transgender identity.
He suspects some people will be surprised by the results of the election.
"They'll be like, 'Oh my God, I didn't know he was a transgender man.' So that's the cool part, and that's the good part about Sparwood," he said.
Sparwood is a B.C. border town just 18 kilometres from Alberta. (Amber Wang/CBC)
Kelloway knows his experience is not universal.
"There's so many people in the world like me that are just abused and live on the streets and I've been so frigging lucky," he said.
He hopes to inspire more members of the 2SLGBTQ+ community to go into leadership positions and inspire other communities to be open to people of different backgrounds.
For Kelloway, the town he once considered leaving has become inseparable from his identity.
"Biologically, my birthplace is Newfoundland. But I was born in Sparwood."
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Amber Wang is an award-winning video journalist and filmmaker with CBC News based in Cranbrook, B.C. She previously worked for BBC World Service, focused on visually driven narratives. You can contact her at amber.wang@cbc.ca.

articles.title: For street food vendors, no choice but to endure high costs
articles.summary: ‘Hindi naman ako nangarap na yayaman ako…. Basta makakain lang tatlong beses sa isang araw,’ says one street food vendor

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – Leah Lobrigo, 48, sells budget meals in Pasig City from Monday to Saturday, 12 hours a day. The cart of her boss is positioned along Alcalde Jose Street, which is near many schools, hospitals, and various establishments.
Among their offerings, a clear favorite is pares, or braised beef served with rice and a bowl of beef broth. It’s staple Filipino street food, perfect for those craving a cheap but satisfying meal.

But as commodity prices shot up due to the United States-Israel war on Iran, even the cost of pares was not spared. From the previous price of P30, Lobrigo’s customers now have to pay P34. She also had to adjust their pares recipe, using lechon kawali or crispy pork belly instead of the more expensive beef.

blocks.caption: STREET FOOD. Customers eat their budget pares meal from Leah Lobrigo’s food cart in Pasig City. Photo by Jelo Ritzhie Mantaring/Rappler

blocks.text: “Naiintindihan naman po nila (customers). Alam naman nila talaga na gano’n kahirap ‘yung buhay, na lalo nagtaas ang bilihin na naman ngayon,” she told Rappler. (Customers understand the situation. They know how difficult life is, especially now that the costs of commodities have gone up again.)
In October, the Philippines’ inflation rate shot up to 7.8% amid higher fuel, electricity, and transport prices. Food inflation eased overall, but rice inflation hit an over two-year high of 20.7%.
To make matters worse, the outlook isn’t looking good with the El Niño phenomenon now considered very strong, and widespread drought expected in early 2027.

If inflation continues to soar in the coming months, Lobrigo worries that it might further push up business expenses and possibly force them to raise prices again, which could lead to fewer customers.

“Parang akin na ‘to eh…. Masaya ako pagka malaki ang benta ko. ‘Pag mahina, parang iba rin ‘yung pakiramdam.” (It’s like the business is mine. I’m happy when sales are up. When sales are weak, it’s a different feeling.)
The daily income of street food vendors is usually volatile.
Ronald Piedad, 39, can earn P500 to 700 daily from selling kakanin, or sweet native delicacies. He sources his products from a local shop in Novaliches Bayan, located in the north of Quezon City.

From there, he pedals his cart daily to Panay Avenue, beside the staircase leading to the Quezon Avenue southbound station of the Metro Rail Transit Line 3. That’s around 12 kilometers away from his residence.

Piedad endures this long travel as he had many competitors in his original area, resulting in sluggish sales even if he went house to house. Still, he has observed a trend of fewer customers at his new spot.
“Nagbago na talaga ngayon…dahil siguro sa higpit-sinturon talaga,” he told Rappler. (Customer behavior has really changed, maybe because they really have to tighten their belts.)

blocks.caption: KAKANIN. Ronald Piedad sells kakanin or sweet native delicacies in Quezon City amid a hot afternoon. Photo by Jelo Ritzhie Mantaring/Rappler

blocks.text: To boost his earnings, he also sells his own palitaw, or flat rice cakes. But he said prices of glutinous rice flour, coconut, sugar, and liquefied petroleum gas or LPG have gone up, hurting his income.
Simply to make ends meet, he might be forced to increase prices, too.

“Hindi naman ako nangarap na yayaman ako…. Basta makakain lang tatlong beses sa isang araw, makakain ‘yong pamilya ko, makabayad din ako sa bahay, gano’n lang, hindi kami papaalisin sa inuupahan namin,” Piedad said. (I’m not dreaming of becoming rich. I just want my family to eat three times a day, and to be able to pay rent so that we won’t be evicted from our house.)

Beside Piedad’s spot is a cart full of skewered street food or tusok-tusok. Mark Ferrer, 32, sells fish balls, kikiam, and squid balls for P20 per stick. The popular kwek-kwek, made by deep-frying hard-boiled quail eggs coated with orange batter, costs P25 per stick.
Ferrer said his boss did not increase the prices of their products to avoid a drop in sales.

blocks.caption: TUSOK-TUSOK. Mark Ferrer prepares his utensils to cook fish balls, kwek-kwek, and other street food items popularly known as tusok-tusok. Photo by Jelo Ritzhie Mantaring/Rappler

blocks.text: Of the total daily profit, 15% goes to Ferrer. On good days, his income could reach around P1,000. But during rainy days, or when classes are suspended, his income could drop to as low as P300.
Top of his mind now: how the Super El Niño will hit his livelihood.

“Magtatiyaga ka na lang talaga kumita ng pera. Kailangan makipagsapalaran ka talaga sa kalye. [Hindi naman puwede] gumawa ng masama para makakain ka lang,” Ferrer said. (You just really have to persevere to earn money. You have to try your luck out in the streets. You can’t resort to crime to put food on the table.)
Lobrigo, a single mother, is still sending three out of her five children to school. While she has a fixed daily income of P660, money is extremely tight.
That’s why during Sundays, her lone day off, she becomes an on-call housekeeper. She is also considering selling dried fish as another source of income.

“Wala nang halaga ‘yong piso natin eh,” Lobrigo said. “‘Yong sinasahod namin…kahit papaano may mararating kung mababa ang mga presyo [ng mga bilihin].” (Our peso practically has no value now. My income could go a long way if only basic goods were cheap.)

blocks.caption: WET MARKET. Pork cuts are displayed for sale at a market in Manila, October 22, 2026. Photo by Rappler

blocks.text: The Department of Agriculture has said that the weakening peso may push up prices of imports such as rice, fertilizer, and other farm goods.
“Don’t panic,” President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. said as the peso recently hit historic lows, seeking to assure the public that the government is “doing everything” to keep prices of goods down.
For ordinary Filipinos like street vendors, however, that may be easier said than done. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Iran executes three men for 'armed unrest' after January protests
articles.summary: It is claimed Hassan Dioband, Hamid Kazemi and Reza Zanganeh were part of anti-government protests earlier this year.

blocks.text: Iran has executed three men accused of carrying out armed unrest during January's anti-government protests, according to state media.

Hassan Dioband, Hamid Kazemi and Reza Zanganeh were accused of throwing Molotov cocktails and grenades, using bladed weapons and firearms, and setting fire to public facilities in the city of Karaj, west of Tehran, Iran's state news agency Tasnim, external reported.
The executions are the latest in a series linked to the protests, including those of people accused of having ties to Israel and the United States.
The number of executions in Iran has increased since US-Israeli strikes on the Islamic Republic began in late February.
The protest movement initially sparked in December last year by the high cost of living rapidly evolved into widespread anti-government demonstrations that peaked on 8 and 9 of January.
Iranian authorities reported more than 3,000 deaths, and blamed the violence on "terrorist acts" orchestrated by the US and Israel.
However foreign-based NGOs gave higher figures and the BBC received multiple accounts from Iranians of security forces opening fire on unarmed protesters.

Tasnim reported that the three men were executed after the Supreme Court upheld their convictions and found them guilty of "participating in operational activities on behalf of the Israeli Zionist regime, the United States and hostile groups".
The damage allegedly included an electricity substation in Karaj which caused power outages in some areas.
Dioband was arrested on 11 January after investigations identified him as a suspect in attacks on public property and incitement to violence.
Ten others accused of taking part in the unrest under his supervision were later arrested.
Reuters news agency reports that they received prison terms of 5 to 10 years.
The latest executions in Iran come after the UN human rights chief Volker Türk said he was alarmed by the rise in death penalties.
In August, Türk said at least 56 people had been executed on national security-related charges since 19 March, including 27 in cases linked to January's nationwide anti-government protests.
Iran is thought to be the world's second-most prolific executioner after China. Last year, it put to death at least 2,159 people, according to Amnesty International.
The human rights group said that was the highest figure on record since 1981 and included 45 executions of suspected dissidents on national security-related charges.

articles.title: DFA rebukes PH officials over China comments, says they must align with Marcos policy
articles.summary: The DFA rebuked other Philippine government bodies and officials over their comments about China, saying that public officials must be aligned with the administration in its response.

blocks.text: Published November 8, 2026 9:34pm

The Department of Foreign Affairs on Sunday rebuked other Philippine government bodies and officials over their comments about China, saying these can undermine diplomatic efforts and that public officials must be aligned with the administration in its response.

"Under the Constitution, the President is the chief architect of Philippine foreign policy," it said in a statement, saying that all government officials, whether civilian or military, are expected to align with President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr.'s policy directions

"Individual officials, agencies or sectors do not independently determine the direction of our international relations. Whatever personal convictions public officials may hold, their public platforms carry institutional responsibilities. They may not pursue preferred approaches toward China, or any other international partner, without regard for the consequences on the government's overall policy," it added.

The DFA issued the statement after Foreign Affairs Secretary Ma. Theresa Lazaro spoke with her Chinese counterpart Wang Yi over the phone—part of a "deliberate effort," the DFA said, to maintain bilateral relations before, during, and after the upcoming ASEAN and APEC summits.
The ASEAN Summit will be held in Metro Manila from November 16 to 18, while the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting will take place in Shenzhen, China, on November 18 and 19.

The DFA called "regrettable" recent statements by various Philippine officials against China's words, as well as its actions in the West Philippine Sea. These statements, the DFA said, "incorrectly merged...documentary evidence, public rhetoric and official diplomatic messaging," and by doing so, "undermine the government's diplomatic approach" and "complicate the work of our diplomats."
"The Philippines' efforts to document and publicize incidents in the West Philippine Sea have established facts, countered disinformation and built international awareness," it said.
"Yet transparency cannot substitute for statecraft. Releasing footage or shaping an online narrative does not, by itself, act as a physical deterrent at sea of a legal strategy."

China claims nearly the entirety of the South China Sea, including the West Philippine Sea, or the part that lies within the Philippines' exclusive economic zone. It has refused to recognize the 2016 arbitral decision that invalidated its nine-dash claim over the sea, and continues to build artificial islands in the area, as well as harass Philippine fishermen.

The Chinese Embassy in Manila, itself a diplomatic institution, has issued several statements about Philippine officials and institutions, in several instances accusing them of being "anti-China" and saying Philippine journalists are "creating hype" against it.
The DFA itself said that the Chinese Embassy's remarks undermine efforts to maintain bilateral relations.

The Embassy has clashed, in particular, with Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr., whom China has banned from entering its territory, and Philippine Coast Guard spokesperson for West Philippine Sea matters Rear Admiral Jay Tarriela.
Lawmakers have sought the recall of Chinese Ambassador Jing Quan over his remarks about China using force in relation to the Philippines.— BM, GMA News
Follow facebook.com/gmanewsonline for real-time news and developments in the Philippines and around the world.

articles.title: UK spent £100m on zombie Brexit border inspection posts
articles.summary: Five of seven facilities in England and Wales never reached operational stage as Tories vacillated over plans to check goods The UK wasted at least £100m in taxpayers’ money to set up zombie Brexit…

blocks.text: The UK wasted at least £100m in taxpayers’ money to set up zombie Brexit border inspection posts that were never used, it has been revealed.

The overall cost of Brexit was put at an estimated £4.7bn by the National Audit Office last year but this included years-long transformation of the software used for customs declarations and other systems built to cope with the UK leaving the single market.

Now fresh information from HMRC on the exact spend on the seven “inland border facilities” has come to light. The sites were built but quickly decommissioned as the Conservative government at the time vacillated over plans to check goods coming in from the continent.

Five of the seven “inland border facilities” in England and Wales never got to operational stage because the Tories decided not to implement all the border checks after concluding food coming from the EU would be the same high standard as it was before Brexit.

blocks.caption: Portsmouth port, which is owned by the city council, spent £23m on building its border control facility. It has never been used at full capacity. Photograph: Martin Godwin/The Guardian

blocks.text: Portsmouth port, which is owned by the city council, spent £23m on building its border control post, which has never been used at full capacity because of the decision to scale back the checks.
The port received £17.1m in government funding for the project, leaving the council to make up the £6m shortfall, which could otherwise have been spent on essential services.

The EU launched all the checks in Calais, Dublin and other European ports from day one as the UK was treated as a “third country” overnight. The most controversial British zombie facility was known as “Dover white cliffs”. Furious residents at the village of Guston were told of the plans for the inland border facility on 31 December 2020, just hours before a “transition year” ended and Brexit was due to be implemented with supposed checks on all lorries coming across the Channel.

Information from HMRC, released under a freedom of information request, shows the facility has so far cost the taxpayer £28m, even though it remains a field. The Department for Transport paid £21m to procure the site and spent a further £7m on initial ground works, including an archaeological survey for any roman remains.

blocks.caption: A site in Guston near Dover, Kent, cost £21m to procure and £7m for ground works, but remains a field. Photograph: Gareth Fuller/PA

blocks.text: Another £17m was spent on a border facility in Birmingham planned at the airport car park. Newly released information shows it cost £11m to build with £6m in “closure costs”.

Another £20m was spent on sites in Warrington and in Ebbsfleet, a town just south of the Dartford Bridge on the Thames estuary. The Warrington site, on the former Shearings holidays coach stop at Appleton Thorn, was chosen because there were no suitable sites available for lorries coming from Ireland into Liverpool, Holyhead and Heysham ports.
Local people vehemently opposed the site at the time. It cost £7m to buy, £9m to build and £1m to decommission.

Another £10m was spent preparing customs and other checks at the former car park at Eurostar Ebbsfleet International train station, which cost £4m to convert into a lorry park and £6m to close, according to HMRC data.

A further £5m was spent on another site tucked away off the M11, just south of Stansted, at North Weald airfield. This airfield was commandeered for the same purpose, to avert congestion on the M25. It cost £3m to build and £2m to close down.

HMRC said Birmingham, Ebbsfleet and North Weald “did not require the acquisition of land”. The decision to build Brexit lorry parks so far from Dover underlined the lack of preparation for the UK’s departure from the EU.
Most of the UK’s lorry traffic is concentrated in Dover, but as a designated area of outstanding beauty it was impossible to conduct the post-Brexit customs and standard checks near the port.

blocks.caption: Costs for the Sevington inland border facility in Kent ran to £154m. Photograph: Gareth Fuller/PA

blocks.text: The UK finally opted for a site 20 miles inland at Sevington in Kent, but even that was last minute. The government previously revealed in a parliamentary question that total capital costs ran to £154m.
This included £30m on the acquisition of farmland between Sevington and Mersham for Britain’s principal Brexit border facility and another £70m to build.
HMRC has revealed through freedom of information that the operational costs have run to £179m, money that would not have been spent had Brexit not happened.

The second site that remains operational is Holyhead – a small site close to the main road to the port which receives goods from Ireland. According to the FoI, the site cost £14m to acquire and another £23m to build.

The figures are separate to investments made by Eurotunnel, the Port of Dover and other ports including Portsmouth. Eurotunnel spent €50m (£41.7m) on building the infrastructure for Brexit checks for trucks and €90m on changes for passengers, including an entry and exit system that has never been activated by the French.

blocks.caption: Mike Sellers, Portsmouth port’s director, said only two trailer checks take place on average each day at the border control post. Photograph: Alicia Canter/The Guardian

blocks.text: The £23m border control post at Portsmouth, the UK’s second-busiest cross-Channel port, now faces an uncertain future. The hi-tech facility was built to government specifications to handle post-Brexit checks. Two trailer checks take place on average each day, according to the port’s director, Mike Sellers, compared with the 80 checks originally envisioned.

He said: “Given the border post’s location within the operational port, ideally we would look to repurpose it rather than demolish it, but it will cost us almost as much to repurpose as to demolish. It was bespoke and built for food import checks and biosecurity, it is not suitable for general warehousing and will have to be changed.”

Sellers and Portsmouth city council’s leader are among the ports calling on the government to provide compensation for the border posts that will become redundant when the UK government’s deal with the EU comes into force.

articles.title: Poland in mourning after shooter with 'ultranationalistic' views killed 6, wounded 15 in Krakow
articles.summary: Poland began two days of national mourning on Sunday, after a 24-year-old man with far-right views drove into a busy central square in Krakow and opened fire, killing six people and wounding 15…

image.caption: A woman speaks with police officers on Sunday over tape marking a cordoned-off area around the Main Market Square following a mass shooting in Krakow, Poland. (Jakub Porzycki/Reuters)

blocks.text: World·New

Poland began two days of national mourning on Sunday, after a 24-year-old man with far-right views drove into a busy central square in Krakow and opened fire, killing six people and wounding 15 others before police shot and wounded him.
The attack happened in Krakow's bustling Main Square at the heart of the city's Old Town

The attack, which Poland’s defence minister described as an "act of terror," happened on Saturday in Main Square in the heart of Krakow’s Old Town. The area is a major tourist hub in the country’s second-largest city.
By evening, mourners had left candles in memory of the victims. The square remained partially closed on Sunday morning as authorities continued their investigation.
Krakow shooting leaves 6 dead, more than a dozen injured
Marie-Ange Collaer wrote on Facebook that she and her family survived the shooting during a trip to Krakow from Brussels.
"We literally ran for our lives and managed to hide from the bullets flying around," she wrote. "Lying on the floor in a shop like in a bad police movie whilst you hear bullets everywhere."
Collaer said her family was "quite in shock" after returning to their hotel but everyone was grateful to be alive.
"We saw a few that did not make it, true horror," she wrote.

items: Polish police say gunman kills 6 in 'act of terror'; 3 more dead found at suspect's home

blocks.text: St. Mary’s Trumpet Call, a traditional five-note melody played every hour from the highest tower of St. Mary’s Basilica on the Main Square, was paused overnight in tribute to the victims. It is the first time the call has been missed since the Second World War.
Attacker’s sister and parents found dead

Four women and two men were killed in the Main Square shooting. Three of the women and one of the men were Polish, Krzysztof Jan Klęczar, the Malopolska regional governor, said on Sunday. A man from the U.K. and a woman from an unidentified foreign country were also among the dead.

The two police officers who stopped the attacker remain in hospital. One of them is still in a coma while the other woke up from a coma, Klęczar said. Officials launched an appeal for blood donations for the benefit of the most seriously wounded policeman.
Cordoned-off areas at Krakow's Main Market Square following Saturday's mass shooting. (Jakub Porzycki/Reuters)
"If it weren’t for the efficient and selfless intervention of these two young men, the number of victims could have been significantly higher," Klęczar said.
Five non-Poles are among the wounded. They come from the U.K., Portugal, Russia, Germany and Austria.
The attacker is also in a critical state, having been operated on multiple times.
There was confusion on Saturday about the shooter’s age, with authorities first saying 24 and later 25. On Sunday they confirmed that he is 24.
The prosecutors said on Sunday they started an investigation for murder and attempted murder of numerous people, including police officers, with the act "constituting a terrorist offense."

Authorities also found three dead bodies at the man’s family home in Ostrowiec Świętokrzyski, a city about 150 kilometers northeast of Krakow. The police said on Sunday they were the bodies of the attacker’s sister, mother and father.
The family members likely died from gunshot wounds, the police said.
The mass killing marks a grim first for Poland
Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński said the attacker holds "very radical" and "ultranationalistic" views.
"Everything indicates that he was fascinated by far-right ideologies," Kierwiński said at a news conference.

Videos posted on social media by witnesses show people running away from the square to take cover on small streets nearby, as well as first responders trying to resuscitate victims. In one video, a police officer is seen repeatedly shooting the attacker, who is lying on the street, only to later slowly collapse to the ground himself.
People stand near candles and flowers left near the Main Market Square in tribute for victims after Saturday's mass shooting. (Jakub Porzycki/Reuters)

Klęczar said the attacker’s father owned over 10 guns legally and that the attacker also owned guns. Local officials in Ostrowiec Świętokrzyski said they seized seven weapons from the family home, bringing the total number recovered to 11, including four found in the possession of the attacker in Krakow or in his car.

Around 411,000 people hold gun permits in Poland, which has a population of 37 million, and interest in gun ownership has been rising, particularly because of Russia's invasion of Ukraine and fear of instability in the region.

Mass shootings are uncommon in Poland. However, in mid-October three attacks at schools in the central province of Mazovia took place within four days, leaving one person dead and many wounded, including children. The young attackers used knives or other sharp objects.

The Krakow attacker’s military gear, guns and overall look were similar to those of other "extreme-right lone actors" committing attacks around Europe, said Kacper Rekawek, a senior researcher at the International Center for Counterterrorism in The Hague.
"We have had attempts before, but now we can say that these kinds of attacks have become successful in Poland."

articles.title: Cop31 must deliver climate progress that people can see is real, host says
articles.summary: High-stakes talks involving 190 countries begin on Monday as world grapples with El Niño supercharged by fossil fuels The Cop31 summit must produce progress, “a tangible outcome ... that people can…
articles.byline: Adam Morton in Melbourne, and Fiona Harvey, Oliver Milman and Graham Readfearn in Antalya

blocks.text: The Cop31 summit must produce progress, “a tangible outcome ... that people can see is real”, its host has said as scores of world leaders and representatives of close to 190 countries gather in Turkey for the UN climate talks.

The high-stakes meeting begins on Monday, as countries around the world grapple with the strongest El Niño weather system on record, supercharged by fossil fuels, which is set to take hundreds of thousands of lives and cause damage costing trillions of dollars.

Friction is expected between the rich and poor worlds over who pays for the impacts of the climate crisis, and the slow pace of cutting greenhouse gas emissions. Temperatures have broken records this year, surpassing the limit of 1.5C above preindustrial levels aimed for in the 2015 Paris climate agreement.

Adão Soares Barbosa, the chair of the Least Developed Countries, a negotiating group of 44 nations, said: “Keeping 1.5C within reach by minimising the duration and magnitude of the overshoot, delivering accessible and predictable climate finance, strengthening adaptation, and addressing loss and damage [caused to poor countries by extreme weather] are not political choices but matters of survival. The credibility of the Paris agreement will be measured not by promises made, but by commitments fulfilled, and lives protected in vulnerable countries.”

blocks.caption: Although the summit is being held in Turkey, the formal negotiations will be presided over by Australia.  Photograph: Sandro Basili/Shutterstock

blocks.text: Unusually, the talks will have dual hosts: they will take place in the Turkish city of Antalya but the formal negotiations will be presided over by Australia, following a compromise reached last year over their competing bids.

Chris Bowen, Australia’s climate and energy minister and president of negotiations for Cop31, told the Guardian in an interview: “We need a tangible outcome focused on implementation [of emissions cuts and finance] that people can see is real. We need progress, it needs to be a step forward on previous Cops.”

Australia also wants a “strong, ambitious outcome” to raise the plight of low-lying countries in the Pacific region for whom the climate crisis poses an existential threat. “We need to finally elevate some of the issues so important to our Pacific family,” Bowen said. “[Only] 0.2% of the world’s available climate finance goes to small island developing states for adaptation, for countries whose very existence is at stake.”
But climate advocates and more than 500 scientists in Australia said Australia must stop approving coalmines and gas projects if it wanted to escape the charge of hypocrisy.

The summit will have a notable absentee, with the US refusing to send a delegation for the second year in a row. The Trump administration wants no part of “extremist climate policies” embraced by other countries, according to a White House spokesperson.

Donald Trump expressed glee shortly before the US midterm elections about the huge profits made by oil and gas companies due to the Iran war, which he started and has caused an increase in living costs around the world. “I don’t give a damn,” the president said at a recent rally in Georgia. “I’m going to say it: we’re making a frickin’ fortune.”

However, a group of 20 Democratic members of Congress have made the trip to Antalya, buoyed by their party’s stunning success in the US midterms last week that will enable them to stymie Trump’s attempts to dismantle pollution rules and withhold financial support for clean energy.

Developing countries and civil society will seek to put climate finance and justice at the heart of the Cop31 talks. Rukiya Khamis, the east Africa programme manager at the 350.org campaigning group, said: “Across east Africa, people are facing the devastating impacts of a climate crisis they did not cause. From prolonged droughts to destructive floods, we are losing homes, livelihoods and access to food and water. Yet the money needed to respond to these impacts remains out of reach for many of the countries and communities most affected. It is fundamentally unjust that those least responsible are being left to carry the greatest costs.”
after newsletter promotion

This summer more than 50,000 people died in Europe due to heatwaves, severe wildfire smoke shrouded swathes of North America and a glacier collapse in Nepal triggered a landslide that caused more than 1,500 deaths, while the El Niño weather event, described as “staggering” by scientists and still to reach its peak, is gathering strength.

However, while the pace of progress on cutting global emissions has been slow, the Iran war has spurred many countries to see fossil fuels as expensive and vulnerable to shocks, while renewables continue to plummet in price.

blocks.caption: Drone view of the Cop31 venue in Antalya, Turkey. Photograph: Murad Sezer/Reuters

blocks.text: Simon Stiell, the UN’s climate chief, said before the talks: “Climate impacts hit every population and every economy harder each year. [But] almost every major economy, and many medium-sized and smaller economies, now see climate action as a central driver of economic growth, jobs, and affordable and secure energy.”

Cop host Turkey also wants more countries to switch to electric technologies, such as electric vehicles and heat pumps, as these are many times more efficient than their fossil fuel counterparts. A target for 35% of global final energy to come from electricity by 2035 will be on the table, but faces opposition from some.

Both presidency countries rely heavily on fossil fuels. Australia is one of the world’s leading exporters of coal and liquefied natural gas. The centre-left Labor government has targets to reach net zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050, and have more than 80% of its electricity generated by solar and wind by 2030, but is off track to meet them.

Labor also faces a political threat from the resurgent rightwing One Nation party, which dismisses climate science. One Nation and the Liberal and National party coalition want to scrap the net zero goal.

The UK energy secretary, Miatta Fahnbulleh, said: “This summer, we all felt it: climate change is here, in Britain, now. No country can tackle it alone, which is why Cop31 matters. The answer to high bills and climate change is the same – more clean, homegrown power, creating good jobs and warmer homes. Cop31 is about Britain’s national interest.”
